comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find the frequency-dependent vasoconstriction data convincing and supported, covering identical claim sets (C6-C8, C52-C69, C76). Both note the quality of electrophysiological and vascular imaging evidence with appropriate controls.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations support the correlation between stimulation frequency, calcium elevation, and vasoconstriction (C79-C84). Both accept the mechanistic link demonstrated in Figure 2.

Full agreement. Both evaluations find the TTX and glutamate receptor antagonist experiments (C86-C88, C92-C94) convincing and well-controlled, supporting action potential dependence and partial glutamate involvement.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations support the single-cell RT-PCR findings (C98-C114) demonstrating COX-1/COX-2 expression and PGE2 synthesis pathway components in pyramidal neurons. Both acknowledge the molecular characterization as convincing.

Strong agreement on COX inhibitor effects (C115-C116, C121-C125). Both find the pharmacological evidence for COX-2/PGE2 pathway convincing. OpenEval additionally covers in vivo validation claims (C117-C120) that peer reviewers address separately.

Agreement on in vivo validation. Both evaluations support the in vivo indomethacin experiments (C117-C120) as important validation of ex vivo findings. Peer reviewers explicitly note this strengthens the conclusions.

Agreement on EP receptor involvement. Both evaluations support the EP1 and EP3 receptor antagonist data (C126-C129, C134-C135). OpenEval covers additional claims about exogenous PGE2 and FP receptors not explicitly discussed by peer reviewers.

Agreement on astrocyte/20-HETE contribution. Both evaluations support the HET-0016 experiments (C145-C147) showing moderate reduction with 20-HETE synthesis blockade, accepting astrocyte involvement as part of the mechanism.

Divergence on NPY/Y1 receptor role. OpenEval finds BIBP3226 data (C148-C150) clearly supported and consistent with intermediary cell involvement. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising concern about logical inconsistency between complete NPY inhibition and claimed direct PGE2 effects.

Agreement on control experiments. Both evaluations support the cortical spreading depression exclusion criteria (C70-C73) and wild-type controls (C75). Peer reviewers implicitly accept these controls by not raising concerns.
